definition: Historical claims to the layer, trended and developed to ultimate, divided by the exposure base (lives, premium or member-months) over the experience period. The experience-rated starting point of a reinsurance price.

The share of a period's ultimate claims that has been reported (or paid) by a given lag. Dividing reported claims by the completion factor gives the ultimate; 1 minus the factor, times the ultimate, is the IBNR / IBNP.

Incurred but not reported: claims for treatments that have happened but have not yet reached the insurer (or TPA) at the valuation date. In medical reimbursement the related IBNP (incurred but not paid) is often the measure in the data.
The expected final total of claims for a period once every claim has been reported and settled: reported claims to date plus IBNR.
The time between a claim's incurred (treatment) date and the date it is reported or paid, usually counted in months. Development triangles are organised by incurred period and lag.
The weight given to a book's own experience against a benchmark or prior when setting a rate; grows with the volume of exposure or claims (classical square-root rule, or Bühlmann).
The expected annual change in claims cost per unit of exposure from the experience period to the rating period: medical inflation, utilisation change and mix. Applied as a factor per year of trend.
Claims divided by premium for the same period and basis (incurred claims to earned premium is the usual pair). The headline measure of a medical scheme's performance.
The part of written premium that belongs to the period: premium spread evenly over the cover period, counted day by day or month by month.
The premium booked when a policy or endorsement is issued, for the whole cover period, before it is earned.
Claims for treatments in the period, whether paid, reported or still to be reported (paid + outstanding + IBNR).
Claims actually settled by the payer or TPA up to the valuation date, by payment date.
One insured life covered for one month; the exposure unit of medical insurance. Twelve member-months are one life-year.
Per member per month: a premium or claims amount divided by member-months, the standard unit price of medical cover.
The amount of risk carried in a period, counted in lives, member-months or premium; the denominator of frequencies and rates.
The year in which a policy or treaty incepts; everything written under that inception is grouped to it regardless of when premium is earned or claims occur.
The twelve months from a policy's inception date; premium and claims of that policy are grouped to it.
The twelve months of a reinsurance treaty from its inception; the period a treaty's price and limits apply to.
Third-party administrator: the company that administers a medical scheme's claims (network, approvals, adjudication) on the insurer's behalf and supplies the claims and membership data.
The insurer (or cedant) whose scheme is being analysed; the owner of the data a TPA administers.
A mid-term change to a policy: lives added or removed, a benefit change, a premium adjustment or a cancellation. Each endorsement is a premium transaction with its own effective dates.

Whether a policy year is the first with this payer (new business) or a continuation of an earlier year (renewal). Decided from the data: an earlier policy year, a renewal link or a contract date before the effective date.
A proportional reinsurance treaty: the reinsurer takes a fixed share of every policy's premium and claims, usually with a ceding commission.
A non-proportional treaty paying the part of each claim (per person or per event) above a retention / attachment point up to a limit, for a premium rated on the whole book.
The amount a claim must exceed before an excess of loss layer responds; the cedant keeps everything below it.
The most a reinsurance layer pays per claim (or per event, or in aggregate); layer width = limit above the attachment point.
An aggregate excess of loss treaty on a book's total claims (or loss ratio) for a year: pays above an aggregate attachment up to an aggregate limit.
The share of ceded premium the reinsurer returns to the cedant under a quota share to cover acquisition and administration costs; may slide with the loss ratio.
The part of each risk the cedant keeps for its own account: the share not ceded under a quota share, or the amount below an excess of loss attachment.
A claim above a threshold chosen for separate treatment (capping, excess pricing, severity fitting): in medical books usually a per-person annual total above a set amount.
The size of individual claims. A severity distribution (empirical or fitted: Pareto, lognormal, Weibull …) describes how claim amounts are spread and drives excess layer prices.
The number of claims (or claimants above a threshold) per unit of exposure; with severity it gives the expected claims cost.
International Classification of Diseases: the diagnosis code on a claim line (ICD-10 chapters A–Z). Used to group claims by condition and to check plausibility against age and sex.
A check that the rows and totals of a stage equal those of the stage before it, less what was removed for stated reasons; a reconciliation that does not tie is a stop.
A check result that blocks the next step: the output is not fit to use until the cause is fixed and the step is run again.
A check result to review before relying on the output: a warning, counted and listed, that does not block the run.
A note written by a check: nothing to fix, recorded for the audit trail.
A stage whose inputs changed after it last ran: its outputs no longer reflect the inputs and the stage needs running again.
The record a run writes of what it did: versions, parameters, inputs read, rows in and out, the time. Read by the page and the dashboard.
A double-click .cmd file in the tool folder that runs one step or a chain of steps; the page runs the same launchers with their non-interactive arguments.
GC's internal AI assistant platform (LenWork). The assists are prompts with attached files that LenAI turns into a mapping, classification or review the tool can read back.
The fixed format a LenAI assist returns in (what it did, counts, decisions, files), so the result can be checked and saved where the tool expects it.
Fictitious records built to the real files' layouts for building and testing; no client data. Shipped only in the admin pack.
